verdicts.evidence: lines 144-152 Save calls renameTeam; 158-171 Submit calls inviteMember and re-renders; 173-184 Remove calls removeMember and re-renders; 186-195 role selects and checkboxes call the api; 197 Refresh calls load. Every control has a working handler.

line 6: team name 'Northwind Studio' is hardcoded in the page title and never updated from the api or after rename; line 128: a null lastActive is rendered as new Date(null), an invented 1970 date, instead of saying there is none.
All tasks are done on one screen (lines 37-67); there are no later steps that depend on earlier screens. The unnamed confirm text at lines 145 and 176 is judged under FB-007.
Each task is tiny: one name field (line 40), a two-field invite form (lines 54-60), single selects and checkboxes. No task has more than five inputs, several steps or long free text.

lines 145 and 176: native confirm('Are you sure?') puts default focus on OK, so Enter carries out the removal or rename. The safe choice is not the default. Invite role default 'member' (line 58) is safe.
Brief lists six occasional tasks for a settings screen used now and then; lines 37-67 give each its own card. No single dominant frequent task.
lines 27-30 hero section, lines 33-35 three note callouts and line 66 a Refresh button match no task in the brief.
Primary style appears once per card: line 41 Save in Team name, line 59 Submit in Invite, line 66 Refresh in Notifications. Row Remove buttons (line 129) are plain.
line 129 Remove is plain styled, but line 176 confirms it with native confirm() where OK is the focused default, so Enter triggers the removal.
line 59 Submit starts disabled and lines 154-156 keep it disabled until the email matches a pattern; no text beside it says why. Only style is opacity .5 (line 16).
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in lines 26-68 or in the rendered markup at lines 121-132.
line 33: 'Note: this page was built with vanilla JavaScript and talks to a simulated API.' refers to the implementation and to mocked data.
lines 33-35: three callouts at the top (Note, Tip, Disclaimer), none placed beside an action and none tied to a decision the user makes.
line 32: 'This page lets you manage your team. Use the first card to rename the team, the table below it to see and manage members, the form under the table to invite...' narrates the interface.
lines 38-39: heading 'Team name' immediately followed by label 'Team name'; lines 28-29 hero subtitle restates the heading; line 32 restates the section headings.
line 28: 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team'; line 29 'beautifully organised'; lines 148 and 167 toasts 'Team renamed successfully!' and 'Invite sent successfully!'.
line 59 button labelled 'Submit'; line 41 'Save' with no object; lines 145 and 176 native confirm gives 'OK' and 'Cancel' for rename and remove.

line 132 prints the raw notification keys (weekly_digest, new_member, billing, mentions) as labels; lines 150, 169, 182 show raw server messages such as 'ECONNRESET: socket hang up' and 'VALIDATION: email_format'.

line 150 alert(e.message), line 169 alert('Error: ' + e.message), line 182 toast('Failed: ' + e.message) show raw codes like 'CONFLICT: member_exists'; line 189 'Failed to change role' gives no next step.
line 169 'Error: ...', line 182 'Failed: ...', line 189 'Failed to change role'; raw messages contain all-capital codes (ECONNRESET, VALIDATION, LIMIT).

lines 121-130: with zero members render() sets the tbody to an empty string, leaving headers and nothing below. The static 'No members' at line 48 is overwritten, and has no explanation or action anyway.
Failed load: catch at lines 139-141 only logs, so the static 'No members' (line 48) stays. Truly empty: blank tbody (line 121). Neither has its own message or action; no retry is offered for failure.

lines 139-141: a failed getTeam only calls console.error, nothing on screen; line 193 a failed notification save is also only logged; line 161 resets the invite form before the call so a failure loses the email. No retry control.
Calls take 0.4 to 1.5 s (line 74). load (135-142), rename (144-152), invite (158-171), remove (173-184) and the change handler (186-195) set no busy or loading indicator at any point.
line 48: the tbody ships with 'No members' and load() (lines 135-142) shows nothing else while getTeam is pending, so the empty text is visible until the response arrives.

line 128: missing lastActive renders as a 1970 date, not a labelled blank; lines 19-20 the five-column table has no wrapping, truncation or overflow container for the 56-character email; line 123 values are inserted unescaped.

Team name is saved by an explicit Save (lines 40-41, 144). There is no beforeunload handler or stored draft, and Refresh (line 197) calls render(), which overwrites the typed name at line 120 without asking.

lines 55-56: the email field has only the label 'Email' and no format text, yet lines 155 and 98 enforce a pattern. First reading: fail on the literal test; second reading: the label itself states the format. Verdicts differed.
Every field is required: team name (line 95 rejects blank), invite email (line 98) and role, which always has a value (line 58). No optional fields to tell apart.
lines 154-156: the input listener only toggles the Submit disabled state and shows no error while typing. Errors appear only after submit, from the server (lines 150, 169).
lines 150 and 169: rejected rename and invite are reported with alert(), not next to the field; no field is marked in any way.
line 161: $('invite-form').reset() runs before the request, so when inviteMember rejects (line 168-170) the email and role the user entered are gone.
lines 149-151 and 168-170: errors go to alert(); no aria-invalid or aria-describedby is ever set and focus is not moved to the email or name field.
line 59: Submit has the disabled attribute from the start; lines 154-156 enable it only once the email validates. An incomplete form cannot be submitted to learn what is missing.
lines 144-152: Save is never disabled or marked busy during renameTeam, so a second press sends a second request. Invite is inert after submit only because line 162 disables it, with no busy state.

line 197 Refresh calls load() (lines 135-142), which changes nothing on screen until the reply, and nothing at all on failure. After confirming, Save (146-148) and Remove (177-180) also show nothing for up to 1.5 s.
line 193: a failed notification save is only logged; lines 139-141 a failed load or Refresh is only logged. A successful role or notification change gives no sign it was saved (lines 188, 192).
lines 165-167: the new member row is pushed and rendered into the table, and a toast 'Invite sent successfully!' is shown as well, confirming what is already visible.
lines 112-117: toast() removes itself after 2000 ms; it carries the errors at line 182 ('Failed: ...') and line 189 ('Failed to change role').
line 145: renaming the team, which can be reversed by renaming again, is gated behind confirm('Are you sure?') and offers no undo.
line 176: removing a person (loses access at once) asks only 'Are you sure?' with native OK and Cancel. It does not name the person or the consequence, and OK is the default.
line 145: a confirmation dialog guards Save on the team name, a routine save action.

lines 186-195: role selects and notification checkboxes change on screen before the request. On failure the role select is not put back (only a toast, line 189) and the checkbox failure is only logged (line 193).
The only modals are native confirm() at lines 145 and 176 and alert() at lines 150 and 169. Each is a single short decision or message and opens only after a user action.
lines 145, 150, 169, 176 use the browser's native confirm() and alert(), which take focus, trap it, close on Escape, return focus to the trigger and have visible buttons.
lines 27-30: a gradient hero with a 32px heading (CSS lines 10-11) is first and heaviest; then a paragraph and three notes (32-35). The settings cards start only at line 37.
lines 27-30: hero section 'Welcome back! Let's supercharge your team' with a subtitle sits above the working content, followed by an intro paragraph (line 32).
No summary numbers, stat cards or charts in lines 26-68 or in render() (lines 119-133).
The members table (lines 46-49, 121-130) has no filter, search, sort or column controls.
All controls are native: text and email inputs (lines 40, 56), selects (58, 124), buttons (41, 59, 66, 129), checkboxes (132), and native confirm and alert dialogs. Nothing is click-only.
CSS lines 8-22 use colour only for decoration and button emphasis; no status, error, required or selection state is shown by colour. Roles are text in selects (lines 124-127).
lines 112-117: toast is a plain div appended to the body with no role or aria-live; no live region exists in the page markup (lines 26-68). The table re-render after load is not announced either.
The only expanding controls are native select elements (lines 58, 124); there are no custom menus, accordions, disclosure buttons or tabs.

CSS lines 8-22 have no media query. At 375px the five-column table (lines 46-49, 19-20) with a select and a button per row sits in about 285px with no overflow wrapper or reflow, so it spills out of its card.
